A.explanation: Gives $\text{A}^{2}$ instead of $\text{A}^{-2}$ because $k = Fr^2/(q_1q_2)$ has charge squared in the denominator.

B.explanation: Rearranging gives $k = Fr^2/(q_1q_2)$, which simplifies to $\text{kg m}^3 \text{s}^{-4} \text{A}^{-2}$ in base units.

C.explanation: Omits the $\text{s}^{-4}$ from force and charge and has the wrong power of ampere.

D.explanation: Omits the time dependence $\text{s}^{-4}$ that comes from $\text{s}^{-2}$ in force and $\text{s}^2$ from charge squared.

hints: Rearrange $F = kq_1q_2/r^2$ to make $k$ the subject as $k = Fr^2/(q_1q_2)$ so you can substitute the units of force, distance and charge.
Recall the SI base units present here: force $F$ is $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, distance $r$ is $\text{m}$, and charge $q$ is current x time, so $\text{A s}$.
Combine powers carefully: the $r^2$ gives $\text{m}^2$ on top while $q_1q_2$ gives $\text{A}^2 \text{s}^2$ on the bottom, so track $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$, $\text{s}$ and $\text{A}$ separately.
walkthrough: Start from $F = kq_1q_2/r^2$ and rearrange for the constant: $k = Fr^2/(q_1q_2)$.
Write each quantity in SI base units: $[F] = \text{kg m s}^{-2}$, $[r^2] = \text{m}^2$, and $[q] = \text{A s}$ so $[q_1q_2] = \text{A}^2 \text{s}^2$.
Substitute into the rearranged equation: $[k] = (\text{kg m s}^{-2})(\text{m}^2)/(\text{A}^2 \text{s}^2)$.
Combine the metre powers: $\text{m} \times \text{m}^2 = \text{m}^3$, giving $\text{kg m}^3 \text{s}^{-2}$ divided by $\text{A}^2 \text{s}^2$.
Combine the second powers: $\text{s}^{-2}/\text{s}^2 = \text{s}^{-4}$, and move $\text{A}^2$ to the numerator as $\text{A}^{-2}$, giving $\text{kg m}^3 \text{s}^{-4} \text{A}^{-2}$.
